saas.name: B2B software
saas.pitch: Sell software to companies that already have too much software. Few customers, real money, very long emails.

social.name: Consumer social
social.pitch: Build the app everyone uses until they don't. Millions of users, pennies each, and the attention span of a goldfish.

marketplace.name: Marketplace
marketplace.pitch: Connect people who want things with people who have them, then take a cut for standing in the middle.

hardware.name: Connected hardware
hardware.pitch: Make a physical gadget with an app. Hardware is hard; it's in the name. Every bug ships in a box.

subscription.name: Subscription
subscription.desc: Everyone pays every month. Predictable revenue, unforgiving churn.

freemium.name: Freemium
freemium.desc: Free for most, paid for a few. Grows fast; the few have to love it.

ads.name: Advertising
ads.desc: Your users are the product. Revenue per thousand users per month.

takeRate.name: Take rate
takeRate.desc: A percentage of every transaction. Squeeze too hard and both sides leave.

deviceSubscription.name: Device plus subscription
deviceSubscription.desc: Sell the gadget near cost, earn on the monthly plan. The razor-and-blades of things with batteries.

engineer.name: The Engineer
engineer.desc: You can build the first version yourself, which is lucky, because nobody else will.
engineer.drawback: Investors find your pitch "thorough". They do not mean it kindly.

operator.name: The Operator
operator.desc: Ex-consultant, MBA, owns three fleece vests. You can sell anything, including things that do not exist yet.
operator.drawback: You cannot write a line of code and your designers can tell.
operator.article: an operator with a fleece vest

designer.name: The Designer
designer.desc: Users love what you make and the press loves how it looks in photos.
designer.drawback: You ship slower than everyone because you keep moving the logo four pixels.

secondTimer.name: The Second-Timer
secondTimer.desc: Your last startup was acquired for an undisclosed sum, which everyone has disclosed. Investors return your calls.
secondTimer.drawback: So does the press, about the last startup.

priya.pitch: Backend engineer who rewrote a bank's ledger over a long weekend. Calm, precise, quietly terrifying in code review.

theo.pitch: Sold enterprise software to a government department that did not need it. Twice. Has never met a stranger.

jun.pitch: Product designer with taste you can't teach and opinions you can't stop. Will die on the hill of good onboarding.

garage.name: Garage
garage.desc: One to five people, one shared extension lead.

startup.name: Startup
startup.desc: Five to thirty people, a real office, and a Slack channel just for dogs.

scaleup.name: Scale-up
scaleup.desc: Thirty people and climbing. You now have meetings about meetings.

coreProduct.name: The thing itself
coreProduct.desc: The minimum viable product. Emphasis on minimum. Required before launch.

onboarding.name: A proper onboarding
onboarding.desc: Users who understand the product in the first minute stay for longer than a minute.

mobileApp.name: Mobile app
mobileApp.desc: Your users live on their phones. Your website currently zooms in sideways.

integrations.name: Integrations
integrations.desc: Connects to the twelve other tools your customers already pay for.

aiAssistant.name: AI assistant
aiAssistant.desc: A chat box that confidently answers questions nobody asked. Investors will gasp. Engineers will sigh.

analytics.name: Analytics dashboard
analytics.desc: Charts that go up and to the right, mostly.

referrals.name: Referral programme
referrals.desc: Give a month, get a month. Your users become your sales team, unpaid.

collaboration.name: Team collaboration
collaboration.desc: Comments, mentions, and the ability to blame a colleague in real time.

payments.name: Payments
payments.desc: Let people give you money without emailing an invoice to someone called Accounts.

darkMode.name: Dark mode
darkMode.desc: Small effort, big applause. Developers will mention it on social media like it cured something.

enterpriseSso.name: Enterprise single sign-on
enterpriseSso.desc: The feature that unlocks the price column with "Contact us" in it.

offlineMode.name: Offline mode
offlineMode.desc: Works on trains, in basements and at your investors' country houses.

search.name: Search that works
search.desc: Currently search finds everything except the thing you typed.

streaks.name: Streaks
streaks.desc: Turns daily use into a mild obligation. Ethically grey, commercially green.

publicApi.name: Public API
publicApi.desc: Let developers build on top of you, then complain about you in your own forum.

trustAndSafety.name: Trust and safety tools
trustAndSafety.desc: Moderation, reporting and the dull machinery that keeps you out of the news.

majorUpdate.name: A major update
majorUpdate.desc: A big, visible release that reminds users you exist. Can be done again whenever the product starts to feel stale.

shipIt.name: Ship it
shipIt.desc: Features first, bugs later. Faster roadmap, more fires.

balanced.name: Balanced
balanced.desc: Runs a tidy team. Steady output, nothing heroic.

stabilise.name: Stabilise
stabilise.desc: Fix what's broken and pay down debt before anything new.

roadmap.name: Own the roadmap
roadmap.desc: Picks the next feature whenever the team runs dry. You stop having to.

polish.name: Polish
polish.desc: Fewer, better features. Slightly slower, noticeably nicer.

vision.name: Big vision
vision.desc: Keynote energy. Hype goes up; so does the tech debt.

steady.name: Steady spend
steady.desc: Spends about 3% of the bank balance a month, efficiently.

blitz.name: Blitz
blitz.desc: Spends about 8% a month. Billboards. Possibly a blimp.

brand.name: Brand
brand.desc: Spends little, builds reputation and buzz over time.

discount.name: Discount to close
discount.desc: More deals, at a lower price. The quarter looks great.

enterprise.name: Go upmarket
enterprise.desc: Fewer, bigger customers who pay more and expect more.

landExpand.name: Land and expand
landExpand.desc: Start small, grow inside accounts. Customers stay longer.

perks.name: Perks
perks.desc: Snacks, wellness stipends, a meditation room nobody uses. Morale up, costs up.

retention.name: Retention
retention.desc: Career ladders and actual one-on-ones. Fewer people quit.

pipeline.name: Hiring machine
pipeline.desc: Two new candidates arrive every month without you lifting a finger.

tenX.name: 10x
tenX.desc: Produces the output of a small team. Knows it. Will be headhunted weekly.

brilliantJerk.name: Brilliant jerk
brilliantJerk.desc: Ships fast. Leaves code review comments that start with "Obviously".

meticulous.name: Meticulous
meticulous.desc: Slower, and the whole team's bug rate drops just by being near them.

shipsFast.name: Ships fast
shipsFast.desc: Moves quickly and breaks things, including other people's things.

cultureCarrier.name: Culture carrier
cultureCarrier.desc: Remembers birthdays, organises the quiz, quietly holds the team together.

flightRisk.name: Flight risk
flightRisk.desc: Has a recruiter on speed dial and a resignation letter in drafts.

loyal.name: Loyal
loyal.desc: Will be here when the lights go out, possibly holding a torch.

exBigCo.name: Ex-BigCo
exBigCo.desc: Very good. Slow to start. Asks where the procurement process is.

empireBuilder.name: Empire builder
empireBuilder.desc: Hires a team for their team. Costs creep upward and so does the org chart.

thoughtLeader.name: Thought leader
thoughtLeader.desc: Posts more than they ship. To be fair, the posts do very well.

operator.name: Operator
operator.desc: Boring and excellent. Spreadsheets reconcile in their presence.

leaker.name: Talks to the press
leaker.desc: Has a journalist's number saved under "Mum".

moonlighter.name: Moonlighter
moonlighter.desc: Has a side project. Has been working on it since about Tuesday.

exRival.name: Ex-rival
exRival.desc: Joined from {{rival}} and knows where the bodies are buried.

mentor.name: Mentor
mentor.desc: New hires get up to speed in half the time.

workaholic.name: Workaholic
workaholic.desc: Productive, and makes everyone else feel they should be at their desk at 10pm.

growthHacker.name: Growth hacker
growthHacker.desc: Your ad money goes further. Do not ask exactly how.

hypeMachine.name: Hype machine
hypeMachine.desc: Can make a bug fix sound like the moon landing.

closer.name: Closer
closer.desc: Signs deals. Rings a bell after every one. The bell is new.

overpromiser.name: Overpromiser
overpromiser.desc: Closes more deals by selling features you haven't built.

securityMinded.name: Security-minded
securityMinded.desc: Reads the changelog of every dependency. Sleeps fine.

burnedOut.name: Running on empty
burnedOut.desc: Came from a startup that died. Hasn't quite recovered.

customerWhisperer.name: Customer whisperer
customerWhisperer.desc: Angry users leave their calls calmer and somehow more loyal.

processLover.name: Process lover
processLover.desc: Introduces a ticket template. Bugs fall. So does the joy, slightly.

remoteFirst.name: Remote first
remoteFirst.desc: No office, lower costs, happier commutes. Collaboration needs more effort.

unlimitedPto.name: Unlimited holiday
unlimitedPto.desc: Generous on paper. People will take less, then suddenly much more.

equityForAll.name: Equity for everyone
equityForAll.desc: Everyone's an owner. People stay longer and care more about the cap table.

hustleCulture.name: Hustle culture
hustleCulture.desc: Weekends are a state of mind. Output up now, burnout up later.

noMeetingWednesdays.name: No-meeting Wednesdays
noMeetingWednesdays.desc: One day a week to do the actual work.

openSalaries.name: Open salaries
openSalaries.desc: Everyone can see what everyone earns. Awkward for a month, fairer forever.

fourDayWeek.name: Four-day week
fourDayWeek.desc: Less output, much happier people, and they rarely leave.

freeLunch.name: Free lunch
freeLunch.desc: There is such a thing. It costs about six percent of your overheads.

cofounder.bio: Signed up for the ride. Owns a meaningful slice of it.

investor.bio: Margot Vell has backed four unicorns and one very public disaster, which she refers to only as "the learning".

rival.bio: Brexton Hale wears a black turtleneck to the gym. He is building the same thing as you, louder.

journalist.bio: Dana Okafor broke the story about the scooter company. She reads every privacy policy for fun.

dentistAngel.name: Dr Ken Albright
dentistAngel.blurb: A dentist who read one book about startups and has a lot of opinions about your mouth-feel.

exFounderAngel.name: Lena Strand
exFounderAngel.blurb: Sold her company to a bank. Writes small cheques and very blunt emails.

supperClub.name: The Tuesday Supper Club
supperClub.blurb: Twelve angels, one shared spreadsheet, a wine budget larger than your seed round.

hollowpine.name: Hollowpine Ventures
hollowpine.blurb: Margot Vell's fund. Patient, well-connected, and will want a seat at the table.

quarryCapital.name: Quarry Capital
quarryCapital.blurb: Fast decisions, hard terms. Their logo is a pickaxe and they mean it.

blueMeridian.name: Blue Meridian Partners
blueMeridian.blurb: Growth investors who only call when your revenue chart has a hockey stick in it.

sovereignTech.name: Northwind Sovereign Tech
sovereignTech.blurb: The technology arm of a very large pension fund. Enormous cheques, enormous due diligence.

burnout.warn1: Two engineers have started eating lunch at their desks. Silently.
burnout.warn2: Someone's status has said "heads down" for three weeks. The heads are not coming back up.
burnout.warn3: The office plant died and nobody noticed for a week. People have stopped noticing things.

scandal.warn1: A reporter followed three of your employees on LinkedIn this week.
scandal.warn2: Dana Okafor emailed asking for "a quick chat about your growth numbers". She attached nothing. That's worse.
scandal.warn3: Your lawyer has started ending calls with "anyway, as I said, nothing in writing".

security.warn1: An engineer mentions the admin password is still "admin". Everyone laughs. Nobody changes it.
security.warn2: Logs show a lot of login attempts from a server in a country none of you can find on a map.
security.warn3: A stranger on a forum is selling "a fun dataset" with suspiciously familiar column names.

boardTension.warn1: Margot's emails have started including the phrase "just checking in".
boardTension.warn2: The board asked for the next meeting to start with "a candid conversation about leadership".
boardTension.warn3: You notice the board has scheduled a call you weren't invited to.

rivalThreat.warn1: {{rival}} has posted three job ads for exactly the roles you have.
rivalThreat.warn2: Brexton Hale gave a keynote with a slide that looked a lot like your landing page.
rivalThreat.warn3: {{rival}} is offering your customers a free year if they switch. Some are asking.
